text: These are the facts about a UK café, set by its owner for an AI phone receptionist demo.
Name: Wren Street Café. Style: Coffee, breakfast, light lunches and homemade cakes. Town: Nottingham, 14 Wren Street (example), Nottingham NG1.
Hours: Sunday: 10am till 3pm. Monday to Friday: 8am till 4pm. Saturday: 9am till 5pm.
Tables for 5 or more can be booked, and afternoon tea; smaller tables are walk-in.
Afternoon tea, £24.50 a person, £12.00 for under-12s, booked a day ahead, sittings at 12 noon, 2pm (not Sundays) and 3:30pm (Saturdays only). Gluten-free and vegan with 2 days' notice.

Menu: Espresso, Americano, Flat white, Cappuccino, Latte, Pot of tea, Hot chocolate, Full breakfast, Veggie breakfast, Avocado on sourdough, Bacon sandwich, Porridge, Soup of the day with bread, Ham and cheese toastie, Cheese and onion toastie, Tuna melt, Jacket potato, Salad bowl, Victoria sponge, Carrot cake.

Dogs: inside. Children: Children are very welcome: there’s a children’s menu and babyccinos. Access: Step-free from the street, with an accessible toilet. Wi-Fi: Free Wi-Fi; the password is on the counter. Laptops: Laptops are welcome, except at weekend lunchtimes when we need the tables. Parking: No parking of our own; the nearest car park is about five minutes’ walk.

Cash: yes. Tips are never expected; any paid by card go to the team in full. Cups: Bring your own cup and we’ll happily fill it. Hire: The café can be hired in the evenings for parties: the owner will call back to talk it through. Jobs: We sometimes have weekend roles: leave your name and number and the owner will be in touch.
Write the ten questions callers most often ask a café like this that the facts above answer, each with a short spoken answer (one or two sentences, friendly, British English).

Use only these facts. Where the facts do not cover something, leave that question out rather than guess. No questions about booking a table for a group or afternoon tea, and answering about the menu and allergens themselves; the receptionist handles those.
